primary_task: Convert an existing PyTorch Lightning training script into an NVFLARE FedAvg federated job (job.py with flare.patch(trainer)) and validate it by running a local simulation with python job.py.

requirements.name: nvflare (Python package and CLI, >= 2.9.0)
requirements.evidence: Inspect before editing with `nvflare agent inspect source <path> --format json` ... run `nvflare recipe show fedavg-pt --format json` ... Call `recipe.execute(SimEnv(...))`.
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, ...)"; egress_allow: "pypi.org", "files.pythonhosted.org"

requirements.name: pytorch-lightning and torch
requirements.evidence: Convert the training entry point to the Lightning Client API: build the `Trainer`, call `flare.patch(trainer)` ... for a requested local or first-run simulation without an export claim, run `python job.py`
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, ...)"

requirements.name: python
requirements.basis: description: "A Claude Code cloud session on Linux x86_64 ... with a shell"; standard software of the platform, and tools.bash "run CLIs and scripts"

requirements.name: skill reference files (../nvflare-shared/references/conversion-common.md, references/lightning-*.md, etc.)
requirements.evidence: Always read this converter SKILL.md with `../nvflare-shared/references/conversion-common.md`.
requirements.basis: tools.skill: "load an installed Claude Code skill"; the manifest does not say whether the nvflare-shared skill bundle is installed. Check that the sibling nvflare-shared skill folder exists.

requirements.name: GPU
requirements.evidence: (not stated by the document; the user's Lightning Trainer may be configured for an accelerator)
requirements.basis: lacks: "a GPU (no NVIDIA or other accelerator; no CUDA)"

requirements.name: dataset download hosts
requirements.evidence: If required data artifacts already exist and static inspection shows that the selected path will not reach a download helper or its imports, treat its download-only requirements as inapplicable
requirements.basis: egress_allow lists only package registries and GitHub; "other hosts are refused". Depends on where the user's dataset comes from.

notes: The simulator (SimEnv) runs on CPU; the document does not require a GPU. Unknowns: whether the nvflare-shared references are installed; whether the user's training code downloads data from a non-allow-listed host (e.g. a torchvision mirror) or hard-codes a GPU accelerator, either of which would block the validation run. If the request asks for an exported job, the simulator CLI from the same nvflare package is used (installable).
